title: No GTA in Space Yet — But These Games Let You Be a Space Outlaw
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it has taken the gaming world by storm. But Rockstar Games has never set one of its open-world games in space. So what can sci-fi fans play if they want a life of crime among the stars? No game has cracked that idea yet, but several space games come close.

Starfield is a massive space role-playing game where you can choose your own path. You can save the galaxy, or you can turn to crime instead. The game has a 'new game plus' mode that lets you start over and live a different life, so trying a criminal career is part of the fun. The game never rushes you to the next main mission, so you can take your time becoming the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems.

The Outer Worlds 2 offers a smaller but still wide-open playground. Its makers, Obsidian, are known for giving players freedom of choice, and this humorous sequel lets you play a star-surfing scoundrel. The main story already puts you on a collision course with powerful corporate interests, so the choice is yours: be a goody-two-shoes or an edgy troublemaker.

No Man's Sky has grown hugely over the years, with customizable space stations, towns full of alien characters, giant kaiju-like beasts, and even fishing. You can command whole pirate fleets and fire on — or steal — every spaceship you meet.

The closest match may be Star Wars Outlaws, from 2024. You play Kay Vess, a Han Solo-like scoundrel dodging stormtroopers and rival criminal gangs, with a wanted system much like the one in Vice City. It jumps between medium-sized maps on different planets, so it never feels quite as seamless as a Rockstar game, but it gets at least halfway there.
why_it_matters: Games shape how millions of players spend their free time, so the search for a space crime game shows what players want next — and which studios might build it.

background_read: An open-world game lets players explore a large map freely instead of following one fixed path.
Grand Theft Auto is a famous series of open-world games about crime in big cities, made by Rockstar Games.
In these games, a wanted system means the police chase the player more and more as they cause trouble.
Space games borrow that idea by letting players fly between planets, take on jobs, and choose whether to follow the rules or break them.
